questions.q: According to the chapter, what did Hong Kong look like to a visitor?
choices: An English town in Kent or Surrey moved by magic
A quiet fishing village with only a few houses
A walled Chinese city full of ancient temples
A Portuguese town just like nearby Macao, across the water
questions.evidence: the appearance of a town in Kent or Surrey

questions.q: What did Passepartout learn at the barber's about the old men dressed in yellow?
choices: They were priests from a temple near the port
They were over eighty, so they could wear yellow
They were rich merchants who owned the junks in the harbour
They were soldiers guarding the government house
questions.evidence: these ancient men were all at least eighty years old

questions.q: Why was Fix so upset when Passepartout found him on the quay?
choices: He had lost his ticket
The warrant had still not come
He was sea-sick again
His money had been stolen

questions.q: What news did the steamer office clerk give them?
choices: The Carnatic was full and had no more cabins left
It would sail that very evening
The Carnatic's repairs would take another two weeks
The Carnatic would stop at Shanghai before Japan
questions.evidence: the steamer would leave that very evening

questions.q: Why did Fix take Passepartout into the tavern?
choices: To tell him everything and get his help keeping Fogg in Hong Kong
To celebrate their going on to America together with a fine dinner and wine
To meet a friend who might have news of the warrant
To get out of the rain while they waited for the boat
questions.evidence: he resolved to tell Passepartout all

questions.q: The place was a smoking-house where many customers "lay upon this bed in a deep sleep" and were called "stupefied." What does "stupefied" mean?
choices: Dazed and unable to think clearly
Angry and ready to fight
Very excited, cheerful and talkative
Hungry and thirsty
questions.evidence: The bed already supported twenty of these stupefied sots.

questions.q: When Fix asked "You have guessed who I am?", who did Passepartout think Fix was?
choices: A police detective from London
An agent of the Reform Club gentlemen
A clerk of the steamship company
A thief who wanted his master's money
questions.evidence: An agent of the members of the Reform Club

questions.q: How much money had been stolen from the Bank of England?
choices: Twenty thousand pounds
Fifty-five thousand pounds
Two thousand pounds
Five hundred pounds
questions.evidence: a robbery of fifty-five thousand pounds was committed at the Bank of England

questions.q: What did Fix show Passepartout to prove he was a detective?
choices: His police badge
His commission
A letter from London
The bank's warrant

questions.q: Which fact did Fix use to argue that Fogg might be the robber?
choices: Fogg had been seen at the Bank of England on the day of the robbery
Fogg left suddenly, without trunks, carrying a large sum in banknotes
Fogg had paid the judge in Calcutta with gold coins stolen from the bank
Fogg had told Aouda that he once worked at the bank
questions.evidence: without trunks, and carrying a large amount in banknotes

questions.q: What did Fix offer Passepartout in return for his help?
choices: A free passage back to France on a fast steamer
A share of the two thousand pounds reward
A job as his assistant at the London police office
His promise that Passepartout would not be arrested
questions.evidence: I will share with you the two thousand pounds reward

questions.q: Why did Passepartout refuse to help Fix?
choices: He had seen his master's goodness and would never betray him
He was sure that Fix was only lying in order to win the bet for the club
He wanted the whole reward for himself, not just a share
He was afraid that Aouda would be angry with him
questions.evidence: I will never betray him--not for all the gold in the world

questions.q: Passepartout says, "I come from a village where they don't eat that kind of bread!" What does he mean?
choices: His village has very poor food
Honest folk there don't do such things
He is very hungry and wants better bread
Bakers in his village use a special recipe
questions.evidence: I come from a village where they don't eat that kind of bread!

questions.q: How did Fix finally keep Passepartout from warning his master?
choices: He locked him in a back room of the tavern
He gave him a pipe that made him fall unconscious
He told the police to arrest him on the quay as a thief
He sent him on an errand to the wrong ship
questions.evidence: Fix slipped one into Passepartout's hand

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Fix reveals he is a detective, Passepartout stays loyal, and Fix keeps him from his master
Passepartout explores Hong Kong and buys gifts for Aouda in the market
Fogg learns about the robbery and agrees to go back to London
Fix and Passepartout become partners in order to catch the real thief
questions.evidence: I am a police detective, sent out here by the London office.
